sentences.text: The known remains of Zatomus include teeth and dermal plates, which are bony scales covering the skin.
American geologist Ebenezer Emmons discovered and described these fossils in North Carolina.
Edward Drinker Cope later named the species Zatomus sarcophagus in 1871, based on fossil teeth he thought resembled those of Megalosaurus, Laelaps, or Teratosaurus.
Zatomus belongs to the unranked order Crurotarsi, the order Rauisuchia, and was once classified within the ancient order Thecodontia, a group of archosaurs that were ancestors of dinosaurs.
Its parent group is Teratosauridae, and it is classified in the family Teratosauridae.
Zatomus lived during the Late Triassic, between 225 and 208 million years ago.
However, the Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Zatomus as the Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
